name: Vilnius Gediminas Technical University
summary: Technical university in Vilnius; 19 bachelor's and integrated degrees open in English, from civil and aviation engineering to IT and business.

ib.text: Entrance score from maths, a science or social-science subject and English, each normalised to your grade scale; 60% overall minimum. Recorded interview. English test unless your studies were fully in English.

lastYear.text: EU apply by 1 August; non-EU by 15 June

programmes.name: Applied Artificial Intelligence
programmes.about: Applying AI algorithms, machine learning and image recognition to control and maintain automatic devices and to build intelligent products; taught in English.
programmes.overview: You start with programming in C, linear algebra, calculus and statistics, then move into machine learning, deep learning, image recognition, language processing, robots and automatic control, using tools such as TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch and SolidWorks. Laboratory work runs through the whole degree, and a semester-long internship in an industrial setting feeds into a two-semester final project in which you design, test and prototype an AI system. Applications range from automated manufacturing and autonomous transport to smart cities. Graduates work at technology and electronics manufacturers, research centres and public bodies, or continue to master's programmes such as Management of Artificial Intelligence Solutions.

programmes.name: Artificial Intelligence Systems
programmes.about: Designing AI systems and understanding machine-learning algorithms, with electronic and software specialisations.
programmes.overview: After a foundation of mathematics, programming in C and Python, algorithms and databases, you study machine learning, software engineering, big data processing, cloud computing and image recognition. In the fifth semester you choose between two tracks: electronic systems, with microcontrollers and signal processing, or software systems, with deep learning and natural language processing. Lab work and integrated design projects run throughout, a semester-long company internship comes in year four, and the degree ends with a bachelor thesis. Graduates become machine-learning, deep-learning or computer-vision engineers, big data architects or analytics developers, and can go on to doctoral study.

programmes.name: Computer Engineering
programmes.about: Creating, programming and securing computer systems, networks and embedded computers, with embedded-computer and computer-systems specialisations.
programmes.overview: The first years combine physics, linear algebra and calculus with programming in C and Python, then electronics, computer logic, computer architecture and signals and circuits. From the fifth semester you follow either computer systems, covering cloud computing, networks and security, or embedded systems and programming, centred on microcontrollers and FPGA. Teaching is lab-heavy, with a practicum in circuit assembly and printed circuit board design, individual FPGA projects, a semester-long internship with a company that designs or services computer systems, and a bachelor thesis. Graduates go into technology firms and IT departments in finance and government, or on to master's study in electronics.

programmes.name: Information Technologies
programmes.about: Designing, running and improving an organisation's IT infrastructure and services, with financial IT and applied IT specialisations.
programmes.overview: The study modules cover corporate IT management, process automation, cloud computing, data centres and the integration of financial information systems, with a specialisation in managing information technologies and security. Teaching is built around laboratory work, problem-based learning and course projects in programming techniques and software development. A 160-hour internship in the final year gives enterprise experience, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates work as business analysts, systems engineers, UX/UI designers, project managers or software developers, and can continue to master's programmes such as Cyber Security Management or Data Science and Statistics.

programmes.name: Mathematics of Modern Technologies
programmes.about: Applying mathematical methods to build and improve technologies and data solutions, from finance to information systems; taught in English.
programmes.overview: The degree centres on statistics and computer science for big data. You begin with calculus, discrete mathematics, linear algebra and C++, then move to probability, algorithms, databases, numerical methods, actuarial mathematics and neural networks. Core modules include machine learning, big data and data modelling. Teaching mixes laboratory work, problem-based learning and software such as Matlab and Python; the final year brings a complex project, an eight-week internship and a two-stage thesis. Electives include cryptography, image processing, quantum computing and financial engineering. Graduates become business analysts, software engineers or programmers, or go on to master's study in data science or AI.

programmes.name: Multimedia Design
programmes.about: Creating visual, audio and interactive solutions for different media with design and programming tools.
programmes.overview: You combine creative and technical work: media production, computer graphics, web programming, game development, animation, audio technologies, image processing, augmented reality and human-computer interaction. Lab sessions use Adobe Premiere, Blender, Unity and similar tools, and course projects include games, websites and video, often in teams. A professional internship and a two-part bachelor thesis finish the degree. An enhanced study group follows a 2+1+1 route with a third year at Goldsmiths, University of London, leading to two bachelor's degrees. Graduates work in interactive media, design studios, advertising and cultural organisations, or continue to master's study such as Digital Graphics and Animation.

programmes.name: Bioengineering
programmes.about: Engineering solutions for biology, medicine and biotechnology, from genetic engineering to sustainable industrial processes.
programmes.overview: The first years build a base in mathematics, chemistry, physics and biology, followed by organic and physical chemistry, microbiology, biochemistry, and molecular and cell biology. Later modules cover chromatography, genetic engineering, bioinformatics, immunology and pharmaceutical biotechnology, with electives in environmental biotechnology. Teaching leans on laboratory sessions and course projects, a semester-long internship in a Lithuanian or foreign company, and a two-semester bachelor thesis with original research. Graduates are prepared for biotechnology, healthcare, food and agriculture research, bioenergy and quality-control laboratories, or for master's study such as Biomedical Engineering.

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.about: Designing machines, mechanical devices and production equipment for users and environments, with a machine-design specialisation.
programmes.overview: You start with chemistry, physics, mathematics, engineering mechanics and materials science, then study mechanisms and machines, machine elements, mechanics of materials, CAD/CAE, cutting processes and 3D and laser manufacturing technologies. In the later years you choose one of three tracks: alternative energy equipment, environmental protection equipment, or machine design. Teaching combines labs and design course projects, an eight-week internship after the third year, and a two-semester bachelor thesis built around a prototype. Graduates work in machine design, production and assembly, energy organisations and research institutions, or start their own design and production firms, and can continue to doctoral study.

programmes.name: Mechatronics and Robotics
programmes.about: Designing and managing mechatronic and robotic systems across mechanics, electronics, automation and informatics, with digital manufacturing.
programmes.overview: After foundations in chemistry, physics, mathematics and engineering mechanics, you study mechanisms and machines, CAD/CAM/CAE, C++ programming, robotics, automatic control, digital automation and industrial logic controllers, ending with a design course for mechatronic and robotic systems. Laboratory work and several course projects run alongside, a semester-long internship takes place in factory settings, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates work in production automation, robotic assembly lines, diagnostics and maintenance in industries such as pharmaceuticals, food and light manufacturing, or continue to master's study in mechatronics, automation or computer engineering.

programmes.name: Medical Engineering
programmes.about: Medical, rehabilitation and orthopaedic technology, biomechanical modelling, CAD/CAM/CAE and 3D printing.
programmes.overview: Mathematics, physics, chemistry and engineering mechanics come first, followed by materials in medicine, biomechanics, human anatomy and physiology, and the design of medical, rehabilitation, orthopaedic and assistive devices and artificial organs. Later modules cover medical equipment, diagnostics, medical robots, rehabilitation technologies and medical psychology. You work in laboratories and on design projects, spend a semester in an internship with a company that designs or makes medical equipment, and complete a bachelor thesis involving research and design. Graduates work in hospitals, rehabilitation centres, medical device and orthopaedic companies, or go on to master's study such as Biomedical Engineering.

programmes.name: Automotive Engineering
programmes.about: Solving transport engineering problems and designing vehicles and equipment, including renewable energy sources, with a vehicle engineering specialisation.
programmes.overview: The first years cover mathematics, physics, chemistry, engineering graphics and materials, then vehicle mechanics, internal combustion engines, vehicle dynamics, hydraulic and pneumatic systems and computer-aided engineering for transport machinery. Later you pick one of five specialisations: automotive transport, railway transport, automotive engineering, mobile machinery or autonomous vehicles. Laboratory work and design course projects run through the degree, and a semester-seven internship places you in a real enterprise. Graduates design vehicles and machinery, or work in transport operations, infrastructure bodies, charging networks and rescue services.

programmes.name: Aviation Mechanics Engineering
programmes.about: Designing, maintaining and improving the mechanical systems of aircraft for safety and reliability, at the Antanas Gustaitis Aviation Institute.
programmes.overview: After mathematics, physics, mechanics and engineering graphics, you study aircraft aerodynamics, structures, materials, functional systems, engines, instruments and flight dynamics. In the middle years you pick electives such as unmanned aerial vehicles, helicopter engineering or space technology. Teaching uses labs, course projects in aircraft design and finite element analysis, and a long internship in an airline maintenance setting, followed by a bachelor thesis. The curriculum is aligned with EASA Part 66 licensing requirements. Graduates work as aircraft technician-mechanics, design specialists or aviation safety regulators, or continue to master's study in aerospace engineering.

programmes.name: Civil Engineering
programmes.about: Designing buildings and structures with modern calculation methods and organising design and construction, with building design specialisation.
programmes.overview: You begin with mathematics, physics, chemistry and engineering graphics, then materials science, mechanics of materials, building architecture and construction technology, before choosing one of three tracks: geotechnics, design of buildings and structures, or design of bridge structures. Core design subjects include reinforced concrete, steel structures, structural mechanics and foundation design. Teaching combines laboratory work in soil mechanics and materials testing, integrated design projects, BIM modelling and visits to construction sites. Graduates design and supervise buildings and structures, run construction processes, work in geotechnics or consulting, or start their own firms, and can continue to master's or doctoral study.

programmes.name: Environmental Technology
programmes.about: Environmental protection technologies, pollution problems and sustainable industrial and urban development, with environmental technology or water management for the thesis.
programmes.overview: The degree starts with environmental processes, calculus, hydrology and engineering graphics, then turns to pollution prevention, air quality, water supply network design, wastewater treatment, waste management and resource recovery, environmental biotechnology and climate change mitigation. Teaching includes laboratory testing, course projects in water and sewer design, field studies at treatment sites, GIS and pollution modelling, and internships with environmental companies. For the thesis you choose environmental protection technologies or water management. Graduates work in environmental institutions, waste and recycling firms, water utilities and consultancies, or continue to a master's.

programmes.name: Business Management
programmes.about: Managing a business project from idea to implementation, with marketing strategies, digital marketing, data analysis, AI and sustainability.
programmes.overview: The early semesters mix quantitative subjects (linear algebra, analysis, probability) with business fundamentals, business law and organisational behaviour, followed by e-business, micro- and macroeconomics, accounting, financial management, digital leadership and entrepreneurship. From the fifth semester you specialise in financial management, business project management or marketing. Case studies and projects focus on the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises, a semester-long internship takes place in Lithuanian or international firms, and a two-semester thesis closes the degree. Graduates work as project managers, marketing specialists, product managers, business analysts or consultants, or start businesses.

programmes.name: Financial Engineering
programmes.about: Creating financial products, managing risk and analysing investments with mathematical, statistical and computer methods.
programmes.overview: A quantitative base of linear algebra, analysis, probability, statistics and Python supports courses in economics, corporate finance, management accounting, behavioural finance, econometrics and financial risk management, plus derivatives such as futures, options and swaps. Teaching combines lectures, seminars and lab work, with a research project, an investment project and a complex financial engineering project. A final-year internship in Lithuanian or foreign companies precedes the bachelor thesis, and an enhanced group can earn an international management accounting certificate. Graduates work in market analysis, forecasting and asset management, or continue to a master's in data science or economics engineering.

programmes.name: Creative Industries
programmes.about: Content creation and communication with digital media across creativity, business and culture.
programmes.overview: You study business communication, creative business, mass communication, media production and sociology, then media studies, research methods, public relations, visual communication, advertising and digital communication, with electives such as film industry, music industry or photography. Learning is project-based, with an integrated project, media projects, a final-semester internship and a bachelor thesis. Students may also work towards a concurrent Bachelor of Arts from Kiel University of Applied Sciences in Germany. Graduates go into advertising, design, film, music, publishing and games, communication agencies and cultural organisations, or work freelance.

programmes.name: Entertainment Producing
programmes.about: Producing entertainment projects, creating entertainment communication content and bringing creative ideas to market, with film and entertainment communication specialisations.
programmes.overview: You study business communication, the psychology of entertainment, mass communication, media production, digital image technology, marketing and public relations. From the fifth semester you choose entertainment communication, with live event scripting and directing and the music and film industries, or film communication, with script writing and film production management. An integrated project in the sixth semester turns a creative idea into a product, and research modules teach quantitative and qualitative methods. A double degree with Kiel University of Applied Sciences in Germany is offered. Graduates work as producers, event organisers, creative project managers, content creators and entertainment marketing specialists.

programmes.name: Architecture
programmes.credential: Long-cycle master's (5 years, Master of Arts)
programmes.about: Five-year programme for architects who shape the human environment, working with specialists from other fields on complex design tasks.
programmes.overview: Design studios form the backbone of the five years, moving from architectural fundamentals, drawing, history and BIM to projects on community, technology, context, heritage and innovation. Alongside them you study theory and composition, urban form, GIS-based urban analysis, tectonics and heritage protection. Studio work uses sketches, computer models and scaled models, with intensive workshops on real briefs, field studies of heritage sites, a two-month internship in a design firm and a master thesis. Graduates work as independent architects, in private firms and in public planning and heritage bodies, and the degree is recognised for regulated practice in the EU.

notes: EU citizens pay €3,250 for business and creative programmes and €4,201 for engineering, IT and technology; non-EU students pay more. The fees page says all EU students can apply for government funding.
Application fee €100, then a €200 registration fee with the first tuition payment; the page says the gap since your last completed education should be at most three years.
